who: Blue Cliff Record, case 16, 1125 · tr. from Chinese
quote: When the mother hen is about to peck, the chick cannot help pecking from inside; when the chick is about to peck, the mother cannot help pecking.
meaning: Student pushes from inside, teacher taps from outside, at the same moment.

quote: When the melon is ripe, it falls.
meaning: When the time is ripe, success comes by itself. No pulling needed.

quote: Where water flows, a canal is formed.
meaning: When everything is ready, the path opens by itself.

who: Baizhang and his student Guishan · Transmission of the Lamp, ch. 9, tr. Chang Chung-yuan, 1969
quote: Master Po-chang asked Kuei-shan to poke the fire pot for burning charcoal; Kuei-shan found none. Po-chang poked deep, pulled out a small glowing piece and asked, 'Is this not a burning piece?' At this, Kuei-shan was awakened.
meaning: The fire was there all along. The teacher knew where to dig.

who: Baizhang · Transmission of the Lamp, ch. 9, tr. Chang Chung-yuan, 1969
quote: To behold the Buddha-nature one must wait for the right moment and the right conditions. When the time comes, one is awakened as from a dream.
meaning: You cannot force waking up. When the moment comes, you suddenly see.

quote: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
meaning: Everything has its own right time. You cannot rush it.

quote: Of all seeds the best are the five kinds of grain, yet if they be not ripe... the value of benevolence depends entirely on its being brought to maturity.
meaning: Even the best seed is no good until it ripens. Goodness too.

who: Marcus Aurelius · Meditations IV.23, tr. George Long, 1862
quote: Nothing for me is too early nor too late, which is in due time for thee. Everything is fruit to me which thy seasons bring, O Nature.
meaning: Things come in nature's time, not too early, not too late.

quote: Peach and chestnut trees bear fruit three years after sprouting, persimmon after eight. Everything takes its own years to come true.
meaning: Every tree fruits in its own time. So does every skill.

who: The Buddha · Samyutta Nikaya 6.1, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato, 2018
quote: After his awakening, the Buddha saw people like a pond of lotuses: some still under the water, some at the surface, some rising above it. So he began to teach.
meaning: Like lotuses, people open when they are ready.
